subject: Pilot econ scenarios — packaging, quantization & caching tradeoffs
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@novusai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics and packaging — NovusAI usage profile attached

Hi Hannah & Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward a 6-week pilot to validate latency and cost for our document summarization workload. I'm attaching our 30-day token trace and a rough QPS forecast. We'd like three things to help our internal decision: (1) a simple set of commercial scenarios (pilot credits vs committed bands), (2) recommended quantization + batching settings for Transformer-XL models (we currently run a 13B variant), and (3) any guardrails you recommend to avoid quality regressions during quantization. Can you propose a couple of packaging options and an estimated cost range? We have procurement on copy at procurement@novusai.com.

Attachments: novusai_usage_profile.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform, NovusAI
samir@novusai.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novusai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics and packaging — NovusAI usage profile attached

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the data. Quick read: your 95th-token-lengths and session QPS make this a good fit for an Optimize pilot (cache + batching focus). High-level options:

- Scenario A — "Conservative Pilot": 10k pilot credits, hosted API, 3% discount on token rates. No quantization by default; we run a canary with 8-bit dynamic quant for non-critical paths. Expected pilot spend range: $8k–$12k.
- Scenario B — "Efficiency Pilot": 20k pilot credits, Dedicated short-term instance for consistent latency, we recommend 4-bit quant + prefix KV caching and continuous batching; expected pilot spend: $5k–$9k (lower token cost but incremental infra cost).
- Scenario C — "Hybrid Commit": 1-month committed band (baseline throughput), deeper quantization profile (mixed-precision + per-layer calibration), and a savings share model. Estimated commit: $30k–$45k monthly, expected unit cost reduction 30–45%.

Technical recommendations: Karthik will include concrete quantization profiles and expected perf numbers. General guardrails: A/B tests on prompt templates, hold-out evals, per-prompt latency SLOs, and rollback policy keyed to model delta on Rouge/EM metrics.

Propose a 30-min sync Tuesday 8/27 10:00 PT to walk scenarios and pick one to formalize. I've attached a quick savings sketch.

Attachments: savings_scenarios_v3.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot economics and packaging — NovusAI usage profile attached

Hi Samir —

Fwding a short technical breakdown (see below). Based on your 13B variant and token distribution:  

- Quantization: Start with per-channel symmetric 8-bit for embeddings and attention weights, then run a narrow sweep to 4-bit (Q4_K_M or similar) on staging with our quant-aware calibration. Expect ~1.8–2.2x throughput improvement at 8-bit and ~3–4x at 4-bit with careful calibration.
- Batching: Use dynamic batching with a max latency budget of 120ms. For your QPS, a 32-token batch size hits 80% GPU utilization; continuous batching with token-aware deadline improves real tail latency.
- Caching: Prefix KV caching will reduce repeated context cost for multi-turn (you have many repeated prompts). We estimate cache hit rate 35–45% based on your traces — that's ~20–30% reduction in token bill for sessions with strong repetition.

Risks and guardrails: Quantization can introduce small token-level changes. We recommend: (1) model diffs with automatic sample-level scoring, (2) a "safety" threshold (e.g., if failure rate > 1% on eval set, auto-fallback to higher precision), (3) staged rollout over traffic slices.

I'll bring a short Jupyter with calibration numbers to Tuesday's sync. Attached: savings_scenarios_v3.pdf (same as Hannah's).

—Karthik

Can you send a short (1‑page) statement of work / pilot terms we can share with legal and procurement after the call? Ideally it should list: scope, pilot length, credit/commit amounts, rollback and data handling clauses, and acceptance criteria.

Also, one ask: can you call out a conservative default (no quant) and an accelerated plan (with quant) so procurement can see both options. Procurement prefers a clear no-change fallback.
